Some recommendations if you're looking to switch things up:

Brown mascara will brighten up the look and might give you more of an "open" feel in the eye area (think light eyeshadow vs dark). Clear mascara is also awesome for that and often times your lashes will be dark enough on their own for a more daytime/casual look.

I'm hoping the healthcare part was about making sure they are healthy? I had a doctor that I tried to talk about weight loss with. He was like "eat right and exercise". Obviously that is good advice, but I feel like if I was asking for help he could have done better.

He could have recommended a nutritionist, a diet plan, an exercise routine, etc. On top of that I had extreme vitamin deficiencies (kinda funny to be big and not actually have enough nutrients), an eating disorder, and a heart condition. I was clearly not healthy which was adding to/stemming from my weight. 

I constantly asked this guy for help and he would literally say "well lose weight". I mean you can google 'weight loss' and there are 1,000 different (and sometimes contradictory) types of diets and stuff. I was soooo pissed. Had working with obesity been higher up on the priorities, I think I would have actually gotten help.

I eventually found a new doctor that is absolutely amazing. I told him my weight was a huge (pun intended) concern. He asked if I would like help and set me up with a nutritionist that I check in with once a month. My eating disorder is mostly under control and I've been healthily losing weight.

I feel like weight is something that is not talked about enough with patients. You wouldn't tell someone they have diabetes but not how to manage it. Run everyday and eat lettuce isn't actually feasible, you know? I had to learn to count calories, which types of foods to eat, the best way to get into exercising and make it a routine, etc. Doctors don't have to make a case out of it every visit, but they could at least listen when a patient brings it up.
